name: Reverse Box Turn (forward half)
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the Box Turn with everything reversed. The turn is to the left; the lead starts forward on the left foot, side on the right, close the left. The mirror image of Box Turn (forward half); no rise. Usually followed by Reverse Box Turn (backward half). Called the Left Box Turn in the American syllabus; the International Reverse Turn is a different, progressive figure. Turn timing from the book (2026-11-17, a box-step study card: the partner going forward "commences to turn" on 1, turns 1/8 between 1 and 2 and 1/8 between 2 and 3; the partner going back turns 1/4 between 1 and 2, "body turns less", and the body completes the turn on 3). Written that way (2026-11-17, to stop the follow's legs crossing on count 2): the bodies turn 1/24 left on count 1 (the turn commencing), 1/8 on count 2 and 1/12 on the close, a quarter in all; the follow, going back on the inside of the turn, points her count-2 foot a further 1/8 (`pointing`); the close's turn is carried back into count 2's foot placement. The lead goes forward, so the couple turns round the follow (the default turning centre) and count 2 is written as her step, as the lead would describe it: 0.5 forward and 0.3 to his left, which for her is 0.5 back and 0.3 to her right. Step sizes, provisional (2026-11-17), chosen by measuring the 3D body solver against the figure checks: count 1 is 0.4 forward and 0.2 to his left. Before this change (0.5 straight forward with no turn on count 1, then her count-2 step 0.4 back and 0.5 to her right) her moving foot crossed behind her standing foot and landed 0.28 on the wrong side of it, so her legs passed through each other, and her foot passed 5-6 cm from his; the figure skipped the "crossed feet" and "partner spacing" checks. Now every check passes and the hips sink at most 0.08 m; the strides are 0.40, 0.71 and 0.39 for the lead and 0.45, 0.58 and 0.20 for the follow.
